places.name: Stanley Park Seawall
places.description: 9km seawall cycling and walking path around 405 hectares of old-growth forest. Mountains across Burrard Inlet, totem poles, Prospect Point with Lions Gate Bridge view.
highlights: Lions Gate Bridge from Prospect Point
Eight Totem Poles — Coast Salish culture

places.name: Granville Island Market
places.description: Vancouver's culinary heart on a former industrial island. 50+ vendors: BC salmon, pastries, artisan cheese, Portuguese custard tarts. Outdoor kayak and False Creek ferry dock.
highlights: Fresh BC salmon and halibut daily

places.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
places.description: 137m suspension bridge, 70m above the Capilano River. Oldest tourist attraction in Vancouver (1889). Treetops Adventure cliffwalk, giant Douglas firs up to 1,000 years old.

places.name: Coal Harbour Seawall
places.description: Flat waterfront promenade from Stanley Park to Canada Place. Superyacht marina, float-plane terminal, North Shore mountains reflected in Burrard Inlet. Vancouver's most scenic walk.

places.name: Gastown Steam Clock
places.description: Victorian-era cobblestone district, Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood. The Steam Clock whistles every 15 minutes. Acclaimed restaurants, architecture tours, and the best selection of independent boutiques.
highlights: Steam Clock whistles Westminster Chimes every 15min
Cobblestone Water Street — oldest in Vancouver

places.name: Kitsilano Beach
places.description: Vancouver's most popular urban beach: 4th Avenue boutiques, Naam vegetarian, and the largest outdoor saltwater pool in Canada. Downtown skyline and North Shore mountains framing the horizon.

places.name: Museum of Anthropology
places.description: Arthur Erickson's masterpiece on UBC cliffs. Largest collection of Northwest Coast First Nations art in the world: Haida totem poles, Gwaii Haanas carvings, Musqueam weavings.
highlights: Haida totem poles in the Great Hall
Raven and the First Men — Haida sculpture
Cliff edge overlooking Strait of Georgia
